title: Second- and third-trimester termination of pregnancy: physiological, neurobiological and psychological adaptation and long-term consequences
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the physical and psychological well-being of women after a late abortion. In Germany, fine diagnostics for the detection of fetal abnormalities are only reimbursed from the 20th week of pregnancy, forcing women to wait until then to make a decision about abortion. This does not take into account the emotional difficulty and potential traumatic impact.
The post-abortion period is still completely unexplored in terms of hormonal adjustment.  After a late-term abortion, many women experience depression, anxiety or persistent grief disorders. It is therefore important to understand the link between hormonal fluctuations  and mental illness following a late abortion. Studies show that the brain undergoes changes after childbirth, but it is unclear whether these occur during pregnancy and are influenced by hormones. It also remains unclear how emotional pain affects physical pain and brain activity.
The study aims to compare early pregnancy termination (first trimester) with that in the second/third trimester. We aim to show that a fine diagnosis in the first trimester brings significant benefits for the well-being of women.
conditions: Termination of pregnancy, affecting fetus and newborn

interventions.name: Patients with a medical indication for TOP (termination of pregnancy) in the 2nd/3rd trimester are recruited and monitored until 24 weeks after the TOP. MRI measurements are carried out before TOP, at 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 weeks after the TOP in order to record the temporal milestones of the adaptation
Women with a medical indication or voluntary TOP in the 1st trimester of pregnancy. Examinations and time points are analogous to arm 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with 1st trimester TOP and patients with 2nd/3d trimester TOP
Exclusion criteria:
History of psychosis or manic episodes, alcohol or psychotropic substance dependence, insufficient knowledge of German, English or Russian. 
Exclusion criteria relating to the MRI examination (metal implants, pacemakers, epilepsy or claustrophobia, etc.)
